questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

What will the minimum external benefit need to be in US$ million to achieve this?
The diagram shows a total utility curve for a consumer. At which point does marginal utility equal zero? C total utility B

options.A: D O quantity

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a consumer’s indifference curves and a budget line for electronic goods and food. If income and prices remain the same, at which point on the diagram will the consumer maximise satisfaction? electronic goods A C B I I

options.D: 2 I O food

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a consumer’s total utility. total utility TU TU TU TU O quantity Which curve would mean that marginal utility is diminishing?

options.A: TU B TU C TU D TU

questions.questionText: Which is an internal economy of scale?

options.A: cheaper loans from a local bank resulting from a merger
options.B: efficient local transport networks
options.C: specialist training facilities provided by a local college
options.D: the reputation of an area for a particular product

questions.questionText: Why might a firm continue in production in the short run even though the price of its product has fallen below its average total costs of production?

options.A: It anticipates a rise in variable costs.
options.B: It expects the fall in price to be temporary.
options.C: It has large fixed costs of production.
options.D: It has no control over the price of its product.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows that a producer increases output from Q to Q .
What is true about economies of scale but not diseconomies of scale?

options.A: They occur because average revenue is increasing.
options.B: They occur because of management policy changes.
options.C: They occur in the short run.
options.D: They occur with decreasing average cost.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be found when comparing the long-run equilibrium outcome in monopolistic competition with that in perfect competition?

options.A: a greater degree of excess capacity in monopolistic competition
options.B: a higher level of profit in monopolistic competition
options.C: a larger number of firms in monopolistic competition
options.D: a more price-elastic demand curve in monopolistic competition

questions.questionText: A government divides a nationalised rail service and sells it to five private companies. The largest of these companies dominates the four smaller companies. How will these changes affect the market structure for rail services?

options.A: It will change from monopoly to monopolistic competition.
options.B: It will create an oligopoly with the possibility of price leadership.
options.C: It will encourage freedom of entry due to lower capital costs.
options.D: It will guarantee ticket prices based on average costs.

questions.questionText: What is meant by ‘real wages’?

options.A: the marginal physical product of labour
options.B: the opportunity cost of labour
options.C: the purchasing power of money wages
options.D: wages net of tax

questions.questionText: The graph shows the percentage growth in average earnings for the UK economy. 2.8 2.8 UK average weekly earnings 2.6 2.6 growth (%) 2.4 2.3 2.2 2.2 2.2 2.1 2.0 Jan April 2017 2017 What is the most likely cause of the pattern shown in the graph?

options.A: a decrease in the supply of labour
options.B: a decrease in the interest rate
options.C: an increase in productivity
options.D: an increase in the size of the labour force

questions.questionText: Which combination of policy changes is most likely to redistribute income from the richest households to the poorest households in an economy? means-tested benefits indirect taxes benefits for everyone

options.A: decrease increase decrease
options.B: decrease increase increase
options.C: increase decrease increase
options.D: increase decrease decrease

options.A: increase in employed workers redundant existing workers

questions.questionText: At present, motorists who drive their cars within area 1 on the map pay a daily congestion charge of $8. X YY Z area 1 aaarrreeeaaa 222 Which car journeys would decrease in number if the congestion charge area were extended to include area 2?

options.A: journeys from point X to point Z
options.B: journeys from point X to point Y
options.C: journeys from point Y to point Z
options.D: journeys from point Z to point Y

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be the biggest contribution to sustainable economic growth in a developed economy?

options.A: a movement of people from rural to urban areas
options.B: an increase in technical training
options.C: an increase in the size of the population
options.D: rising consumer credit levels

questions.questionText: When calculating national income by the income method, what would not be included?

options.A: income from abroad
options.B: profits of private sector businesses
options.C: rent from the ownership of land
options.D: transfer payments

questions.questionText: Which changes to basic income at points W and X might be included in the calculation to reach disposable income? basic income add W = gross income subtract X = disposable income W X

options.A: bonus payment direct taxes
options.B: bonus payment indirect taxes
options.C: cost of living direct taxes
options.D: cost of living indirect taxes

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with no government sector, when will an increase in investment spending generate the largest increase in equilibrium national income?

options.A: when households have a high level of autonomous consumption
options.B: when households have a high level of compulsory saving
options.C: when households have a high marginal propensity to consume
options.D: when households have a high marginal propensity to save

options.B: 2.4 trillion 0.897 66.8 million

questions.questionText: What is an example of a Keynesian macroeconomic policy that would reduce cyclical unemployment?

options.A: an increase in government spending on new infrastructure such as roads
options.B: an increase in government spending on retraining workers
options.C: a reduction in the rate of tax on imports
options.D: a reduction in the rate of tax on goods and services

questions.questionText: The graph shows changes in the unemployment rates in countries X, Y and Z over the period 2000 to 2010. All three countries faced recession between 2008 and 2010. unemployment rate % 8 X Y Z 2000 2005 2008 2010 year Which conclusion can be drawn from the graph about the period 2000 to 2010?

options.A: All three countries experienced an upward trend in unemployment over the period.
options.B: Country X had the highest number out of work in 2010.
options.C: In terms of unemployment, the country least harmed by the recession was country Y.
options.D: The total number out of work in the three countries was higher in 2010 than in 2000.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the annual percentage (%) change in employment and output in the UK private sector between 2000 and 2012.

Recently, among European countries the Netherlands had the highest percentage of part-time employees and an average working week for all employees of 32 hours. Greece had a smaller percentage of part-time employees but an average working week for all employees of 41 hours. Which conclusion may be drawn from this information?

options.A: Greece has a higher percentage of its workforce in full-time employment than the Netherlands.
options.B: On average part-time employees work longer in Greece than in the Netherlands.
options.C: The average working week in Greece for full-time employees is longer than in the Netherlands.
options.D: There are more part-time employees in the Netherlands than in Greece.

questions.questionText: In 2017 a report suggested that by 2030 automated robots could threaten 33% of existing jobs in the UK, compared with 38% in the US and 21% in Japan. Manufacturing and retail jobs faced the greatest threat. Which type of unemployment is illustrated in the above paragraph?

options.A: demand-deficient unemployment
options.B: frictional unemployment
options.C: seasonal unemployment
options.D: structural unemployment

options.A: B rate of rate of interest interest LP LP LP

questions.questionText: Which macroeconomic policy is most likely to be used as a long-run means of reducing inflationary pressures?

options.A: exchange rate policy
options.B: fiscal policy
options.C: monetary policy
options.D: supply-side policy

questions.questionText: What may prevent a government achieving a faster rate of growth of real GDP?

options.A: Consumption and investment expenditure are interest rate elastic.
options.B: The consumer price index is below its target set by the central bank.
options.C: The economy is operating on the long-run aggregate supply curve.
options.D: There is a large negative output gap in the economy.
